name: org.onthebooks/onthebooks
title: On the Books
description: Local law in US towns: municipal code passages and answers cited to chapter and section.

tools.name: find_town
tools.description: Look up a US town, city, village, borough, township or county in the On the Books library of local codes (9,700+ municipalities, all 50 states) and get its id for the other tools. No sign-in needed. Read-only.

name.description: The place name, e.g. "Maplewood" or "Austin, TX".

state.description: Optional state, as a two-letter code or full name, to narrow same-named towns.

tools.name: search_code
tools.description: Search one town's municipal code (its local ordinances) by keyword and get the matching passages in the code's own words, each with its chapter and section, plus the link to the town's official published code. No sign-in needed, no model call. Leave "town" out to search every town's code at once (needs a connected pass or a key). Read-only.

query.description: A few keywords for the rule, e.g. "fence height", "backyard chickens", "short-term rental permit".

town.description: The town's id from find_town, e.g. "maplewood-nj". Omit to search all towns (connected pass or key required).

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask a plain-English question about one town's local law ("Can I keep chickens?", "How tall can my fence be?") and get a written answer cited to the chapter and section of the town's code. Takes 10–40 seconds. Signed in with a pass (or with a key), each answer counts as one of the pass's questions. Without, it returns the matching passages of the code instead of a written answer. Changes nothing except that count.

town.description: The town's id from find_town, e.g. "maplewood-nj".

question.description: The question, with the facts that matter (property type, zone, what is being built or done).

tools.name: compare
tools.description: Ask the same question of 2 or 3 towns and get one comparison, each town's rule cited to its own code. Needs a connected pass (sign in) or a key; counts one question per town. Takes 20–60 seconds. Changes nothing except that count.

items.description: The town's id from find_town, e.g. "maplewood-nj".

towns.description: Two or three town ids from find_town.

question.description: The question to put to every town.
